label: Lamborghini L539 6.5 L V12 (Aventador LP 700-4)
based_on: Lamborghini L539 6.5 L V12, Aventador LP 700-4 (2011 specification)

sources.what: Automobili Lamborghini press kit 'Lamborghini Aventador LP 700-4' (launch, 2011), 28-page PDF on Lamborghini's newsmarket press site: engine chapter (L539, 60-degree V12, bore, stroke, displacement, compression, valve timing control, dry sump, intake with four throttle valves and two flaps, three-into-one exhaust with four pre-catalysts, power and torque) and technical data table. Manufacturer document.
GTspirit report of Lamborghini's Aventador S release, 19 December 2016: maximum engine revs raised from 8350 to 8500 rpm, VVT and VIS modified. Motoring press; quotes the release.
Ward's Auto on the Aventador S: 'maximum safe engine revs from 8,350 to 8,500 rpm'. Trade press.
kfz-tech.de Lamborghini V12 page: Aventador firing order 1-12-4-9-2-11-6-7-3-10-5-8. Technical encyclopedia, no source given.
Supersportiva: Lamborghini V12 firing order 1-12-4-9-2-11-6-7-3-10-5-8 and the practice of printing it on the engine. Enthusiast site.

notes: Modelled variant: the L539 as launched in the Aventador LP 700-4 in 2011, rated 515 kW (700 hp) at 8250 rpm and 690 N m at 5500 rpm. Sourced from Lamborghini's launch press kit: 60-degree V12, bore 95 mm, stroke 76.4 mm, 6498 cc, compression 11.8, four valves per cylinder, electronically controlled inlet and exhaust valve timing, an intake with four throttle valves and a variable path ('two flaps, several channels and one bypass'), four three-into-one exhaust manifolds each with a pre-catalyst, two main catalysts and a two-muffler casing switched by valves, published power and torque. The 8350 rpm maximum (used as limiter and redline) is from two press reports of the 2016 Aventador S release, which raised it to 8500. The firing order 1-12-4-9-2-11-6-7-3-10-5-8 is from two enthusiast pages (kfz-tech.de, Supersportiva), not a Lamborghini document. ASSUMED: cylinders 1-6 on one bank and 7-12 on the other, both numbered from the front, and a conventional six-throw crank with opposite cylinders sharing pins; with that numbering the order fires evenly every 60 degrees (engsim pins confirms the shared pins and even intervals). Also assumed: each three-into-one collects three adjacent cylinders of one bank (front three and rear three), which puts cylinders 240 degrees apart on each manifold. Estimated, not sourced: rod length (145 mm), valve diameters (38 and 32 mm) and lifts (11.5 and 10.5 mm), one fixed cam timing (inlet 20/60, exhaust 60/20 degrees at 1 mm lift) standing in for the variable timing, intake runner length (300 mm, diameter derived), plenum and throttle sizes (derived defaults; one throttle of the default size stands in for four), header primary length and diameter (450 mm, 42 mm), the length from the manifolds to the cross-over (secondary_len 1.6 m), idle 950 rpm, everything else left to derived defaults (cross-over, pipes, muffler, flywheel inertia). friction_scale 0.85 and heat_q 2.55e6 were set inside their ranges, away from the limits. Valve sizes, runner length and secondary length were fitted to the published figures. Not modelled: the variable intake (one fixed runner length, so one set of intake resonances; the real flaps exist to smooth the torque curve, and the model's curve is weaker below 4500 rpm, about 425 N m at 3000 and 550 at 4000), the cam phasing, the exhaust valves that switch between the two mufflers (one muffler path is modelled), the catalysts as separate elements, the dry-sump system and the cylinder-by-cylinder ion-current combustion monitoring.
